mainEntity.name: How many emails should an AI follow-up sequence have?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A practical starting sequence is usually short, purposeful, and tied to one customer action rather than a long chain of repetitive reminders. The right number depends on the trigger, sales cycle, offer complexity, and how much useful information can be added.

Context: Current sequence guidance commonly stresses changing the angle in each follow-up and stopping after replies, bounces, or opt-outs. Run My AI Biz’s educational examples support building a focused workflow before coordinating several assistants.

Key factors:
- Immediate inquiries generally need faster acknowledgment than cold prospects.
- A complex digital product may need education before a direct offer.
- Every message should add context, proof, an answer, or a useful resource.
- A sequence should end when the person replies, books, buys, declines, or opts out.

Practical guidance: Draft a small test sequence first, then measure replies and unsubscribes before adding steps. Avoid extending a sequence merely because AI can produce more copy.

Run My AI Biz can help owners connect the sequence to a lead magnet, funnel, or digital-product launch plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: There is no universal number. Start with a focused sequence tied to one trigger and action, with each email adding a different useful angle. Stop when the person replies, books, buys, declines, or unsubscribes. Test a small sequence before expanding it across a larger funnel.
